claim: New York City has real estate worth as much as Mexico produces in a year
caveat_shown: Department of Finance market values are the city's own estimates and lag sale prices.

claim: New York City has as many millionaires as the Bay Area
caveat_shown: The Bay Area here is San Francisco plus Silicon Valley, a region rather than a city. Both counts mean at least $1 million in liquid, investable assets.

claim: New York City has as many Wall Street jobs as Alphabet has employees worldwide
caveat_shown: New York City's figure is preliminary.

claim: New York City has a Queens whose economy is the size of Ethiopia's
caveat_shown: Holds for 2024 only. Ethiopia devalued the birr and the IMF puts its 2025 dollar GDP at $109 billion, a quarter lower, so the two have already parted company.

claim: New York City has a Staten Island whose economy is the size of Mongolia's
caveat_shown: Both figures are 2024. The IMF puts Mongolia 7 percent higher in 2025.

claim: New York City maintains as many bridges and tunnels as Rhode Island has bridges
caveat_shown: The two sides count different things: the city figure mixes bridges with tunnels, the federal figure is bridges over 20 feet on public roads, and neither includes the big Port Authority and MTA crossings.

claim: New York City has as many fire hydrants as London
caveat_shown: London's hydrants are split across four water companies; New York City's belong to one utility. Both figures are rounded.

claim: New York City has as many miles of water main as Los Angeles
New York City runs as many public buses as Hong Kong's whole franchised fleet
New York City gives as many bus rides a year as the European Union has people
caveat_shown: New York City Transit buses only; the MTA Bus Company adds about 120 million.

claim: New York City is served by airports that carry as many passengers as Istanbul's
caveat_shown: Newark is in New Jersey and Stewart is in Orange County, so this is the regional airport system rather than airports inside the city.
